output.summary: Bulb-growing herbaceous flowering plants, true lilies are mostly native to temperate and subtropical parts of the Northern Hemisphere. They bear large, often fragrant flowers in many colours, commonly marked with spots or brush-like streaks. Their starchy bulbs are edible, although those of some species are too bitter to eat.
output.edibilityNote: Starchy bulbs are eaten as root vegetables; some species are too bitter. Dried bulbs may flavour soups or be reconstituted and stir-fried.
